BUILDINGS.name: Individual Buildings
BUILDINGS.url: See LRPOLYS and OS Open Map Local
BUILDINGS.updatefrequency: Should be updated when LRPOLYS or OS Open Map Local are downloaded
notes: Individual building outlines are created from Land Registry polygons and OS Open Map Local using the following process:
• Land Registry polygons and the buildings layer of OS Open Map Local are intersected
• intersection geometries that are points of linestrings are eliminated
• MultiPolygons are replaced with a building for each polygon
• Polygons less than 10M2 are eliminated
• Duplicate polygons are eliminated as far as possible
• The largest polygon in a land registry polygon has its dwelling count set to 1, others are set to 0
• Polygons that contain the seed of an important building got the OS data are marked as important buildings and not dwellings
• Previously recorded manual data is merged where dwelling counts have been set manually, so that
• corrections applied manually are maintained even when the data is regenerated.

EPCS.name: Energy Performance Certificates
notes: The url can be used to get a dataset with 2 files certificates and recommendations in csv format.
These are loaded into the database using scripts 9_loadEPC_CERTS.js and 10_loadEPC_RECOMMENDS.js.
There may be more than one certificate for an address, for our purposes we are only interested in the latest EPC for an address,
so a table containing only the latest EPC for each address is produced.
Each EPC has a postcode. A summary table at postcode level is produced from the EPCs for that postcode.
Postcode summaries lying within each area are then accumulated.

Defined as all roads within the Teignbridge boundary plus trunk roads (defined by the trunkroads flag) and
The network also contains road nodes, which are needed to navigate the network.
Road nodes have been processed to generate a table OA_ROADNODE which relates nodes to output areas.

TrafficCounts.name: Dft Traffic Counts
notes: Traffic counts are available from Dft for motorways, A roads and some minor roads.
These have been downloaded from Dft using a script, and are imported to
the database using a script.
This dataset gives traffic flows from 2000 to 2018 at each count point,
it should be possible to use this to derive a model of flows in the major road network,
but it is questionable how useful this is to us in creating a baseline for areas such as parishes.
Perhaps we could at least assign transport emissions to areas, but this may not be fair because many trips
are through journeys which have nothing to do with the area.
To date no processing or presentation of this data has been done. A preliminary look suggests that
there are some areas that have seen significant traffic growth.

description: ONS Population data from 2018. This is a value for each age in years up to 89, then 90+
This has been processed into the following age groups:
• Under 18
• 18 to 65
• 66 and over
Data is then presented as a table with columns for Males, Females and Total
Rows represent each age band.
Data is published at Census 2011 output area level,
in most cases parishes and wards are made up of a number of whole output areas.
In a few cases a parish is too small to make an output area,
in these cases population is apportioned according to the number of dwellings.
Gas and electricity meter readings are summarised at census 2011 Lower Super Output Area level (LSOA).
Gas meters are also available at postcode level,
gas meter readings whose postcode lies within the area are summed for the area to give energy.
Some meters have been excluded from the postcode level data to avoid identifying individuals,
when calculating emissions a correction is applied to ensure that postcode level readings within an LSOA add up to the LSOA total.
For areas that don't correspond with output area intersections are formed: OA_PARISH, OA_WARD, OA_DEVON_WARD.
On each of these intersection tables LSOA_PROPORTION is calculated as the ratio of dwellings in the area to dwellings in the LSOA.
Electricity meter readings are calculated for OA, PARISH, WARD and DEVON ward are calculated using LSOA_PROPORTION.
Then these are summed for higher level geographies.
Emissions are calculated by applying the ratio of district emissions to energy consumption for the district for each fuel group
Other Fuel energy and emissions are apportion using the ratio of EPCs with other heating sources in area to that in district.
